items.quote: It outlines appropriate and fair processes for handling complaints of sexual violence or misconduct.
A student who has experienced sexual misconduct can make a complaint to the College’s Director of Student Services (see below), or any employee of the College with whom the student feels comfortable.
This policy does not replace the criminal process. Any individual who is a survivor of sexual misconduct or who witnesses criminal behaviour is encouraged to report that behaviour to the RCMP.
Where the Director receives an actionable complaint, they will initiate an investigation within five business days.
At any time before or during an investigation, the College may take interim measures to ensure the well-being of any member of the College.
This policy applies to sexual misconduct involving a student of the College, both on and off campus, that is in any way related to the student being a member of the College community
If the outcome of the investigation is that the allegation of sexual misconduct is unsubstantiated, the College will promptly notify the individuals involved.
Building a culture of consent, as defined in this policy, by offering ongoing education, awareness and training to the college community about preventing and responding to sexual misconduct.
